text:
Ava: Heads up — eval-dispatcher started requeuing shards at scale this morning, causing a retry storm and CI evals to timeout. Stack: eval-harness -> dispatcher -> worker-pool. Queue depth jumped ~200 -> 12k in ~3m.

Diego: Oof. Any obvious exception patterns in the dispatcher logs?

Ava: Pattern is worker acks missing, dispatcher marks shard as failed and increments retry count, then requeues. We hit max concurrency and spectacular thundering. Sample log: 
```
2026-02-14T09:12:07Z dispatcher INFO shard=eval-129 state=assigned worker=worker-47
2026-02-14T09:12:12Z worker WARN shard=eval-129 processing-timeout
2026-02-14T09:12:12Z dispatcher ERROR shard=eval-129 ack-missing, requeue attempt=1
2026-02-14T09:12:13Z dispatcher ERROR shard=eval-129 ack-missing, requeue attempt=2
```

Rohan: Are workers crashing or GC pausing? Any OOMs on the worker side?

Ava: No OOMs in the time window. CPU spiking on some workers, but many workers showed normal CPU and still didn't ack. Suspect the ack path flakiness + aggressive requeue backoff=0.

Claire: CI spike correlated? I saw several test runs fail with "timeout waiting for eval result" around 09:15.

ci-bot: [build/eng-evals #482] failed — timeout after 15m waiting for evaluation results.

Diego: Two separate issues could amplify: (1) Dispatcher currently uses simple immediate requeue on ack-miss (no jitter), (2) Retry count is global per-shard across dispatcher restarts, so thundering restarts re-enqueue same shard many times.

Rohan: Proposed quick mitigations:
- Add exponential backoff + jitter on requeue attempts
- Make dispatcher ack-timeout configurable per-model (some long-running evals need larger windows)
- Add safeguard: stop requeueing a shard if queue-depth > threshold and escalate instead of flood requeues

Ava: +1. Also can we make the dispatcher use "sticky assignment" for N retries to the same worker where possible, to avoid reassigning to a cold worker pool?

Claire: For CI specifically, we can short-circuit: if total requeue attempts exceed X in CI runs, mark the build flaky and abort extra requeues to give tests deterministic failure rather than cascading timeouts.

Diego: I dug into code — current requeue impl: 
```python
# eval_dispatcher.py (current)
def on_ack_timeout(shard_id):
    increment_retry(shard_id)
    enqueue(shard_id)  # immediate requeue, no jitter
```
We should change to: 
```python
def on_ack_timeout(shard_id):
    r = increment_retry(shard_id)
    delay = min(60, (2 ** r) + random.uniform(0, 1))
    schedule_enqueue(shard_id, delay)
```
This should dampen retry storms.

ops-bot: Note: increased queue depth triggers autoscale; beware of unintended GPU spin-up costs.

Rohan: Also, metric definitions are misleading: current metric "eval_dispatcher_requeues_total" counts enqueue calls but does not label by reason (ack-miss vs worker-fail vs capacity). We need labels: reason, model, env (ci|prod). Dashboard is currently summing everything so we missed the ack-miss signal.

Ava: Good catch. We should add a histogram for ack latency too, and a gauge for inflight shards per-worker.

Claire: I can patch the dashboard: add panel for requeue_rate{reason="ack_miss"} and inflight_per_worker heatmap. Also show CI vs prod split.

Diego: CI wiring: one of the causes for flakiness is that our CI agent times out waiting for the Harness but doesn't surface dispatcher metrics in the build page. We should add a small step in CI to push dispatcher health (queue depth, requeue_rate) as artifacts. That way flakes show the cause.

Ava: Agreed. For short term:
- Diego: deploy jittered backoff change to staging today (hotfix branch)
- Claire: add dashboard panels and CI artifact step
- Rohan: add metric labels and ack-latency histogram
- Me: add safety gate: if queue_depth > 10k, stop requeueing and post a ticket/alert to #eng-oncall

Claire: FYI adding the dashboard panels will require the new metric labels; I'll keep panels templated to ignore missing labels until Rohan ships.

Diego: Quick PR link: https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/2371 (wip) — includes backoff + jitter + configurable per-model ack-timeout.

Ava: Nice. Anyone opposed to doing a controlled rollback window after deploy to staging (15m watch)?

Rohan: I'll add test in eval-harness unit tests to simulate ack timeouts and assert no more than N requeues per 10s. Also add integration test in CI that fails if requeue_rate spikes above threshold.

ci-bot: Scheduled test run: build/eng-evals #483 queued.

Diego: After staging looks good we'll promote to prod during low-traffic window. Also we should triage any retained shards created during the storm: add a cleanup job to deduplicate shards older than 1h with retry_count > 5.

Ava: Thanks all. If you hit more weirdness, ping @ops oncall and drop logs here. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Alert created: #incident-eval-requeue-176543 created. Thread will be copied to incidents channel.
